explanation.en: أَب، أَخ، حَم، فُو، ذُو show case with long vowels instead of harakat when they are mudaf: raf' with و (أَبُو), nasb with ا (أَبَا), jarr with ي (أَبِي). Watch the same kunya change through this story: قَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ (subject) but ذَهَبَ إِلَى أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ (after a preposition).

examples.en: Abu Hanifa (subject → أبو) said to him.
…to his teacher Abu Hanifa (after إلى → أبي).

why.en: The kunya must show jarr with ي after a preposition — treating أبو as frozen is one of the most common learner errors.
As subject it must be أبو (raf' with و).
